newsitem.title: UK: Physical and paper Brent slide a few notches lower.
newsitem.headline: Physical and paper Brent slide a few notches lower.

text.p: A cluster of physical Brent trades on Friday echoed weaker outright forward prices and showed the market slackening further as many had expected, traders said.
Wet trade was dominated by a major seen offering earlier, who then appeared later to gobble up the majority of the day's physical Brent cargoes, including two from today's paper chain.
February 22-24 and 23-25 loading cargoes were sold at March paper +15 and +16 cents respectively, both turning wet today
They were sold by a major while the remaining three dates from the chains were kept by a U.S. trader, giving it a battery of cargoes loading between February 22-26.
Earlier the day's major buyer also picked up February 19-21 and 21-23 loaders at March +25 and +20 cents respectively.
Similar slippage was seen for Forties, with a 570,000 cargo moving at Dated Brent +46 cents for February 22-24 after talk earlier in the week around +50 cents.
Talk on the other grades was seen scarce with slim pickings for later month cargoes matched by a lack of interest from refiners weathering a downturn in margins.
Paper spreads responded sluggishly to the weaker tone as outright prices recovered slightly in late talk.
March Brent was around 15 cents down at $21.50 a barrel.
March/April traded at +38 and +39 cents as a major sold the spread and late bids were pegged around +35 cents. The more dormant April/May was assessed around +29/33 cents.
The day's wet action pushed nearer Brent CFDs down with next week traded at +9 cents and bids at +5 late.
The Mediterranean was quiet with refiners stepping back from the Urals market in the expectation of the grade hitting a dollar discount to Brent in the next trade.
The region's key buyer of the grade remained withdrawn after its last purchase on Monday.
